extractionNotes: No synthesized tonal ramps: the implementation defines semantic colors, and this documentation records implemented values only.
The schema-v2 frontmatter owns primitive tokens; this sidecar holds extension tokens and actual component CSS.
Component preview dashes are placeholders, not sample financial results.
This documentation pass inspected source only; it does not claim a new browser or accessibility audit.

narrative.overview:
The Shipping manifest world makes financial work feel like a clear, ruled working document. Navy navigation frames a mist-green canvas and warm-white work areas. Teal identifies actions and selection; compact system typography keeps attention on assumptions and their consequences.

The interface is dense enough for analysis while keeping labels, units, help and values separate. Conventional controls, restrained borders and tabular quantities carry the identity. The shipped visual assets are authored inline SVG marks, icons and financial geometry; there are no shipping raster assets or external font dependencies.
keyCharacteristics: Ruled source-and-use pairs and aligned financial quantities.
Warm-white work areas within a quiet green canvas.
Conventional controls, explicit units and plain English.
Intrinsic wrapping with local scrolling for wide financial data.

rules.name: The Meaningful Color Rule
rules.body: Use teal for actions, selection and distributions; use warning ochre for contributions and cautions, and danger red for validation or negative table values. Keep explanatory text beside color-coded states.

rules.name: The Numeric Alignment Rule
rules.body: Use tabular numerals for financial quantities and right-align comparable table values. Preserve signs, currency and the stated cash-flow basis.

rules.name: The Local Scroll Rule
rules.body: Let forms and summaries wrap to the available width. Preserve wide financial tables and chart geometry in their own keyboard-focusable scrolling regions.

rules.name: The Flat Work Surface Rule
rules.body: Keep work panels, tables and summaries flat. Reserve shadows for the toast and modal dialog.

dos: Do use sentence-case labels, visible units and specific help that explains how an assumption affects the model.
Do pair invalid fields with written errors and keep unavailable results explicit.
Do preserve semantic tables, captions, scoped headers and a text equivalent for the chart.
Do use authored SVG icons with visible action labels or an accessible name for icon-only controls.
Do keep selected states, keyboard focus and storage feedback visible.
donts: Don't introduce decorative imagery, marketing claims or ornamental display typography into this working interface.
Don't shrink the whole page to fit wide financial tables; keep horizontal scrolling local to the data region.
Don't replace actual financial states with a generic success score or a color-only investment verdict.
Don't add card shadows or animated chart entrances to the flat working surfaces.
